summary: Phase 3 (True AI SDR Agent) fully verified. Added 33 new tests in /app/backend/tests/test_phase3.py covering the background pipeline, versioned prompts, per-piece regeneration, AIDecision persistence, /leads/status-counts, and /analytics/ai. Also updated Phase 1+2 tests (backend_test.py + test_integrations.py) to POLL /api/leads/{id} after POST /api/leads (which is now async and returns in <1s). Full suite is 79/79 passing (100%) in ~127s wall clock. Verified end-to-end: (a) POST /api/leads returns in <3s with processing_status='pending' and qualification.score=None; (b) polling shows pending → analyzing → qualified within ~15-25s; (c) final qualification has ALL new fields (business_type, icp_match bool, icp_match_reasoning, urgency, decision_maker_probability int 0-100, score_explanation, action_reasoning); (d) recommended_action always within {'Book Demo','Call Immediately','Send Personalized Email','Add to Nurture Campaign','Reject Lead'}; (e) lead.outreach has subject+first_email+linkedin_message+followup_email (all non-empty strings); (f) legacy generated_email {subject,body} still populated for backward compat; (g) full integration activity chain (created→qualified→email_generated→hubspot_contact→hubspot_company→hubspot_deal→slack_notified→slack_high_priority when score>=85) preserved after background processing; (h) /leads/status-counts returns exactly {pending,analyzing,qualified,failed} as ints and reflects live counts; (i) /leads/{id}/decisions returns >=2 AIDecision rows (qualification+outreach) each with id/owner_id/lead_id/decision_type/prompt_name/prompt_version(int)/model='gpt-5.2'/input_summary/output(dict)/latency_ms(int>0)/status('success'|'fallback'|'error')/at; (j) /prompts returns exactly 2 items (qualification+outreach) both v1 with non-empty templates; /prompts/{name} 200; /prompts/invalidname 404; PUT bumps v1→v2 and template reflects on GET; reset bumps to v3 and restores default; (k) /prompts/qualification/test returns full qualification JSON and inserts an AIDecision (verified via analytics.total_ai_decisions delta); /prompts/outreach/test with supplied qualification returns all 4 outreach pieces; (l) regenerate with type=first_email|linkedin_message|followup_email touches ONLY the targeted field (other two remain byte-identical), records the correct decision_type (regenerate_email|regenerate_linkedin|regenerate_followup); type=all regenerates all three; type=invalid → 422; unqualified lead (score=None) → 400; unknown lead → 404; other-user's lead → 404; legacy /regenerate-email alias still regenerates first_email only; (m) /analytics/ai returns full shape with correct types and owner isolation (fresh user gets empty analytics); prompt_versions dict contains 'qualification' after any successful qualify call.

minor.issue: Spec says 'if qualification not supplied, backend runs qualification internally first, then outreach'. Actual implementation passes an empty {} to generate_outreach when qualification is missing (server.py:174-177 — `qual or {}`), it does NOT run qualification first. If a caller omits qualification the LLM will receive empty industry/intent/etc context. Consider running self.qualify() first when qualification is None.

AIService.generate_outreach() always returns ALL 4 pieces (subject/first_email/linkedin_message/followup_email). Even when type=first_email or type=linkedin_message, the LLM generates all 4 but only 1 field is persisted. This wastes ~5s of LLM latency + tokens per single-piece regeneration. Consider a lighter prompt for single-piece regen.

Legacy leads with processing_status=None are silently bucketed as 'qualified' (server.py:305-306: 'else: counts[qualified] += ...'). Documented in code as 'legacy leads' but the choice conflates real qualified leads with unprocessed legacy rows. Consider a 'legacy' or 'unknown' bucket.

_run_pipeline runs sequentially: qualify (~5-6s) → outreach (~5-6s) → integrations. Total 12-15s. Consider gather() for qualify+outreach when they don't depend on each other's output (they do — outreach needs qualification — so this only helps if you accept parallel speculative generation).

action_items: (minor) Decide whether /api/prompts/outreach/test should internally run qualification when it is missing — spec says yes, code says no. Either update spec or update endpoint.
(minor) Consider a lightweight single-piece regeneration prompt so type=first_email doesn't burn LLM tokens generating linkedin+followup that will be discarded.
(minor) Add a 'legacy' bucket to /leads/status-counts instead of silently rolling legacy leads into 'qualified'.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:_run_pipeline (line 181-255) is 75 lines with 3 try/except blocks and mixed responsibilities (state transitions + qualify + outreach + integrations + activity appending). Consider extracting each phase into a helper on AIService/Orchestrator to keep pipeline flow readable.

server.py:regenerate (line 348-388) reconstructs the Outreach model and legacy GeneratedEmail on every call. If two regenerate calls race (same lead), the second one wins based on last-write. Not a data-corruption risk since output is idempotent, but no optimistic locking. Acceptable for MVP.

ai_service.py:generate_outreach always calls the LLM with the FULL outreach prompt regardless of decision_type (regenerate_email, regenerate_linkedin, regenerate_followup, outreach, test). This means per-piece regeneration wastes ~75% of LLM output. Consider passing decision_type into the prompt or using a targeted single-piece template.

prompt_store.py:get() seeds a default on first read. If two coroutines call get() simultaneously for the same (owner,name) pair (e.g., first login), you could insert two docs (no unique index on (owner_id,name)). Add a unique compound index or use $setOnInsert upsert.
prompt_store.py:update always increments version even if template didn't change. Consider skipping the version bump when new template == existing template to avoid confusing history.
models.py:Qualification — score field is Optional[int] with no upper/lower bound validation. LLM could theoretically return score=200 and it would persist. Add Field(ge=0, le=100).

models.py:AIDecision — decision_type is a str, not a Literal. All the string constants ('qualification'|'outreach'|'regenerate_email'|'regenerate_linkedin'|'regenerate_followup'|'test') are enforced only by convention. Consider Literal for compile-time safety and OpenAPI schema clarity.

server.py:analytics_ai treats decisions.status='fallback' as failure for qualification_success_rate. If LLM ever hits transient errors, fallback path is engaged which produces valid heuristic output BUT is counted as non-success. Consider separating 'llm_success_rate' vs 'qualification_success_rate' (any output produced).
server.py:/leads/status-counts uses cur async iteration for aggregation but returns immediately after the loop — no ordering guarantee for parallel writes. Acceptable but tests should be aware.

rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no bugs found. Regression failures on first full-suite run were EXPECTED: Phase 3 changed POST /api/leads from sync (returned fully-qualified lead) to async (returns immediately, pipeline runs in background). Updated Phase 1+2 tests to poll for terminal state instead of asserting on the immediate POST response. This is a test maintenance fix, not an app fix — the behavior change is intentional per Phase 3 spec ('POST /api/leads returns instantly').
